absent: Which build options select each stack padding value and each empty versus active syscall stub variant.
How compatibility type conversion handles signed versus unsigned and long versus short forms.
What populates trust domain system information and how seam calls signal each error.
How patched text synchronization and the copy helper operate.
How thermal and early trust domain hooks behave when enabled.
How cycle to nanosecond parameters are computed and used.
How translation flush helpers for broadcast, mask trimming and global promotion decide.
How thread processor number is maintained and how restart data is consumed.

findings.text: System call wrappers obtain up to six arguments from saved user registers in fixed order, using bx for the first slot then cx and dx and si and di and bp for slots two through six, with a compatibility narrowing conversion applied on 32-bit paths before forwarding to typed handlers.

Zero argument entry aliases directly to its implementation, multi argument entry forwards register derived values to a sign extended layer, and conditionally defined entry provides a weak fallback that reports not implemented when no definition exists; all stub declarations permit injected errors classified as errno.

Each application binary interface family provides two variants of its stub and conditional helpers, one that expands to a concrete per ABI entry and one that expands to nothing, allowing builds to enable or omit 64-bit, 32-bit, 32-bit compatibility and x32 compatibility entries independently.

Definition helpers create the layered handler triple for compatibility and native calls, declaring sign extended and implementation forms plus both relevant ABI stubs, with the middle layer converting long values to declared types and for native multi argument forms also validating and protecting the result.

Trust domain extension status uses bit 63 for error and bit 62 for non recoverable, defines software error as error plus bits 47 through 40, and derives codes for invalid state with offset FFFF0000 in hex plus general protection and undefined opcode trap numbers.
Success is reported as numeric zero while the no entropy condition is reported as hexadecimal 8000020300000000.
Feature word zero bit 1 indicates preserving behavior across updates and bit 18 indicates that base pointer is not modified.
Version numbers are rendered as three decimal components with the last component zero padded to two digits in major minor update order.

Virtualization exception information holds exit reason then exit qualification then guest linear address then guest physical address as four 64-bit fields, followed by instruction length and instruction info as two 32-bit fields.
In the examined configuration early initialization and halt helpers perform no action and early virtualization exception handling always declines, indicating the feature is compiled out.
Runtime update capability is determined by testing the preserving bit in the features word of the supplied system information structure.

Trust domain bookkeeping keeps a root page pointer plus a count and array for control pages plus a count for virtual processor control pages, while virtual processor bookkeeping keeps a root page pointer plus its precomputed physical address plus an array for control pages.
In the examined configuration module initialization and system disable perform no action, guest key identifier count is zero, machine check detail and system information queries return null.

Version uses three 16-bit numbers, features use one 64-bit word, memory region descriptor uses five 16-bit limits and sizes, control sizes use three 16-bit values, configuration uses fixed masks and counts plus leaf tables, handshake uses one 16-bit value, and the top aggregate combines version with features and region and control and configuration.

Patching supports at most 5 bytes per site, with breakpoint and return each 1 byte using CC and C3 in hex, call and near jump each 5 bytes using E8 and E9, short jump 2 bytes using EB, and displacement 4 bytes.
Generated instruction storage can be viewed either as a raw byte array sized to the maximum or as a packed pair of operation code plus signed displacement.
Size lookup returns the architectural length for the five recognized operation codes and zero for any other value.

Instruction generation requires the caller buffer to be at least as large as the operation needs, conceals pointer values from constant folding, stores the operation code, and for multi byte forms computes a relative offset from the end of the instruction to the destination, rejecting short jumps whose offset does not fit in a signed byte.
Single instruction generation reuses one shared static slot and returns its address, so consecutive calls overwrite the previous result and concurrent callers race.

Breakpoint emulation helpers directly update saved state: jump sets the instruction pointer, push decrements the stack pointer and stores a word, pop loads a word and increments the stack pointer, call combines push of return address with jump to target, return combines pop with jump to the popped address.

Condition evaluation interprets low condition encodings by testing overflow carry zero sign and parity flags through a small table, interprets high encodings via signed comparison of sign versus overflow with optional zero inclusion, then applies inversion for odd encodings.
Conditional jump emulation adds the supplied displacement to the fall through address only when the saved flags satisfy the requested condition, then jumps to the resulting address.
In the examined configuration local vector table setup and processor thermal initialization perform no action.
Kernel stack top reservation has four build dependent values: sixteen, eight, twice eight, and zero.

Thread metadata starts with low level flags and system call work as two unsigned long words plus a 32-bit synchronous status, with an additional 32-bit processor number when symmetric multiprocessing is enabled; initial state clears flags.

Thread flags occupy bits sixteen through twenty seven for store bypass, indirect branch, cache flush, floating point load, CPU identifier and timestamp restrictions, input output bitmap, speculation update, forced trap, single step, block step and 32-bit address mode, each with a corresponding single bit mask; lazy reschedule polling and single step support are advertised as present.

Context switch work base combines restrictions on CPU identifier and timestamp with block step, store bypass and forced speculation update; one build adds indirect branch mitigation while the other does not, previous task work adds user return notification with optional input output bitmap handling, next task work equals current switch work, and stack warning threshold is one eighth of thread size.

With frame pointers enabled the helper walks saved frame links between supplied stack bounds and accepts only objects fully inside the caller region beyond saved registers, otherwise reporting bad stack; without frame pointers it reports a distinct not stack value.

Compatibility execution uses value 2 to mark active 32-bit system calls on 64-bit builds and value 4 to mark registers modified by a 32-bit tracer; restart capture copies the current synchronous status into restart storage.
Presence of an architecture specific new execution setup hook is advertised by defining its name to itself.
Cycle to nanosecond conversion parameters consist of 32-bit multiplier and shift plus 64-bit offset totaling sixteen bytes.

Entropy helper returns the hardware timestamp counter when that feature is available and otherwise delegates to a generic fallback; one build variant aliases the name to itself to indicate an architecture override.
Timestamp counter read issues the hardware read instruction and combines low and high halves into a single 64-bit result.

Translation lookaside buffer flush wrapper derives an unmap shift hint from gather state and for partial unmaps forwards the recorded range, otherwise requesting a full flush, passing through table free indication.

Range flush advances the address space generation under a barrier, then selects broadcast for global address spaces, remote multicast when other processors share the mask with optional mask trimming and global promotion, or direct local execution when only the current processor is involved, finishing with secondary translation invalidation notification.
The local only flush path asserts interrupts are enabled before disabling them around the actual invalidation and re-enabling afterwards while remaining pinned to the current processor.

Instruction generation traps if the supplied buffer is smaller than required for the operation and traps if a short jump displacement cannot be represented, preventing emission of truncated encodings.
Push and pop emulation directly dereference the saved stack pointer and adjust it by machine word size, relying on a gap reserved by exception entry; incorrect stack values corrupt memory.
Each examined header defines a unique inclusion guard macro to ensure single inclusion within a translation unit.
Presence of an architecture specific copy helper for patched text is advertised by defining its name to itself.
Presence of an architecture specific translation flush helper is advertised by defining its name to itself in one variant.
